newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia govt, unions in standoff as protests spread.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia govt, unions in standoff as protests spread.

text.p: Bolivia's government broke off talks with trade unions on Thursday as strike action against an agrarian reform bill snowballed.
A group of local farmers launched a hunger strike on Wednesday. This was followed on Thursday by a call for an indefinite general strike, although local media said support was limited so far.
Activity was expected to grind to a halt on Friday in the affluent western district of Santa Cruz, where business leaders have called a parallel 24-hour protest.
Talks between authorities and trade unions broke down on Wednesday, mainly over the government's insistence on creating an agrarian agency which could decide land ownership changes.

"The strikes prevent us from meeting to discuss issues on the agenda and to resume meetings ... related to the bill," said Presidency Minister Guillermo Justiniano in a letter to the COB trade federation.
The letter was released simultaneously with a statement declaring the strikes illegal.
But COB leader Edgar Ramirez blamed the government for blocking a truce and warned that protests would spread.
President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada on Thursday complained of "pressure from the extreme right" in a reference to businessmen who rejected a proposed tax on land ownership and investments.
The lower house of Congress, controlled by the ruling party, said on Thursday it would immediately start debating the bill.
A week ago more than 10,000 rural workers marched on La Paz after a 360-mile (600-km), month-long trek to demand guarantees for their properties.
